Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant changes you're experiencing as a new mother, and I'm here to support you in any way I can. As part of our conversation today, I'll be using the EPDS to help us understand how you're feeling and to identify any areas where you might need some extra support.

The EPDS is a tool that helps us screen for symptoms that can be common during the postpartum period, and it's a way for us to check in with you and make sure you're doing okay. It's completely confidential, and everything we discuss today will be kept private. I want you to feel safe and supported in our conversation, and I'm here to listen without judgment.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us get a better understanding of your emotional well-being over the past week. I'll ask you each question, and you can share your thoughts and feelings with me. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll be here to support you throughout our conversation.

Let's get started with the first question. I want to ask: Over the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Honestly, it's been really tough for me to find the humor in things lately. I mean, I used to love watching comedies and laughing with my friends, but now it feels like it's been ages since I've really laughed. Sometimes my baby will do something cute, and I'll smile, but it's not the same as really laughing. I just feel so overwhelmed and tired all the time, and it's hard for me to enjoy the things that used to bring me joy. Even when my partner tries to make me laugh, it feels forced, and I just can't seem to shake off this sadness. I do still enjoy some things, like spending time with my baby, but it's just not the same as it was before. Everything feels so serious and stressful now, and it's hard for me to find the funny side of things. (pausing, looking down) Sorry, it's just really hard for me to explain... I feel like I've lost myself a bit since having the baby.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

(sighing) To be honest, not really. I mean, like I said, my baby will do something cute and I'll smile, but it's not like I'm really laughing or feeling carefree. Most of the time, I'm just worried about whether I'm doing everything right, and if my baby is healthy and safe. It's hard for me to relax and enjoy the moment when I'm constantly thinking about all the things that could go wrong. And even when my partner or family members try to make me laugh, it feels like I'm just going through the motions. I don't really feel like myself anymore, and it's hard for me to find joy in things like I used to. (looking down, fidgeting with hands) I just feel so anxious and stressed out all the time, and it's hard for me to see the funny side of things when I'm feeling so overwhelmed.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(shaking head) Not really. To be honest, I've been feeling really discouraged and sad a lot of the time. I used to love planning things and looking forward to them, but now it just feels like everything is so much work and stress. Even things that I used to enjoy, like going for a walk or meeting up with friends, just feel like too much effort now. I feel like I'm just going through the motions of taking care of my baby and trying to keep everything together, but I'm not really looking forward to anything or feeling excited about it. (pausing, looking down) Sometimes I'll think about things that I used to do before the baby, like going out for dinner or seeing a movie, and it just feels like that's a whole different life now. I don't know, it's just hard for me to feel enthusiastic about anything when I'm feeling so tired and overwhelmed all the time. (sighing) I just wish I could feel like myself again, you know.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nodding) Yeah, that sounds like me. I feel like I'm always blaming myself for something. If my baby is crying, I think it's because I'm not doing something right. If I'm feeling tired, I think it's because I'm not managing my time well enough. If my partner is stressed, I think it's because I'm not supporting them enough. (sighing) It's like, no matter what happens, I always seem to find a way to blame myself. And it's not just little things, either. I'll think about all the things I could have done differently during the pregnancy or during labor, and I'll wonder if I somehow messed things up. (looking down, voice dropping to a whisper) I just feel like I'm not good enough, like I'm not doing this whole mom thing right. And it's hard for me to shake that feeling, no matter how many times my partner or family members tell me that I'm doing a great job. (pausing, taking a deep breath) I guess it's just really hard for me to be kind to myself right now.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(nodding vigorously) Oh, yeah. That's me all the time. I worry about everything. Is the baby eating enough? Is the baby sleeping enough? Is the baby healthy? Is the baby safe? (listing off worries on her fingers) I worry about SIDS, and about the baby falling off the bed, and about the baby getting sick. I worry about not being able to soothe the baby when they're crying, and about not being able to figure out what's wrong. (taking a deep breath) And it's not just about the baby, either. I worry about my relationship with my partner, and about how we're going to manage as new parents. I worry about going back to work, and about how I'm going to balance everything. (shaking head) It's like, my mind is just constantly racing with all these worst-case scenarios, and I feel like I'm always on edge, waiting for something to go wrong. (looking up, eyes wide with anxiety) And the thing is, I know it's not rational. I know that I'm doing the best I can, and that my baby is healthy and safe. But it doesn't matter. The worries just keep coming, and it's hard for me to calm myself down and relax. (fidgeting with hands) Sometimes I feel like I'm just waiting for the other shoe to drop, you know? Like, something's going to go wrong, and I just need to be prepared. (sighing) It's exhausting, really.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(nodding, taking a deep breath) Yeah, that's happened to me a few times. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing their diaper, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out. (placing a hand on her chest) It's like, my chest will get all tight, and I'll feel like I'm having trouble breathing. And it's not just when I'm alone with the baby, either. Sometimes it'll happen when my partner is there, or when we're out in public. (looking down, voice dropping to a whisper) It's so embarrassing, because I feel like I'm losing control or something. And the worst part is, it's not even like there's a reason for it. The baby will be fine, and everything will be okay, but I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of fear and panic. (shaking head) It's hard to explain, but it's like my body is just reacting to some kind of invisible threat or something. (pausing, taking a deep breath) And then, after it passes, I'll just feel so exhausted and drained. Like, I've been through some kind of ordeal or something. (sighing) It's really scary, because I don't know when it's going to happen, or how to make it stop.
Things have been getting on top of me

(exhaling heavily) Oh, yeah. That's an understatement. I feel like everything is getting on top of me, all the time. Taking care of the baby, managing the household, trying to keep up with my own self-care... it all just feels so overwhelming. (shaking head) I feel like I'm drowning in a sea of responsibilities, and I don't know how to keep my head above water. Some days, just getting out of bed and getting dressed feels like a monumental task. (laughing humorlessly) I mean, I used to be a functioning adult, you know? I used to be able to get things done, and take care of myself, and now... now it just feels like everything is too much. (looking down, voice cracking) And the worst part is, I feel like I'm failing. I feel like I'm not doing enough, or doing things right, and that's just... (trailing off, struggling to hold back tears) Sorry, it's just really hard for me to admit that I'm not coping as well as I thought I would. (wiping away a tear) I just feel so... overwhelmed. All the time.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nodding, tears welling up in her eyes) Yeah, that's me. I've been having a really hard time sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up all the time, although that's definitely part of it. It's just... I feel so unhappy and anxious all the time, and it's hard for me to wind down and relax at night. (sighing) I'll lie in bed and my mind will just start racing, thinking about all the things I need to do, and all the things that could go wrong, and... (shaking head) It's just hard to turn it off, you know? And even when I do finally fall asleep, I'll have these vivid dreams that are just so stressful and overwhelming. (rubbing her eyes) I feel like I'm just not getting any rest, even when I am sleeping. And it's not just the lack of sleep that's the problem, it's the fact that I'm just so... unhappy. (voice cracking) I feel like I'm just going through the motions of being a mom, but I'm not really enjoying it, and that's just... (trailing off, struggling to hold back tears) Sorry, it's just really hard for me to admit that I'm not feeling the way I thought I would be feeling after having a baby. (wiping away a tear) I thought I would be happy and fulfilled, but instead I just feel... lost and overwhelmed. (looking down, voice barely above a whisper) And the fatigue is just... constant. I feel like I'm running on empty all the time, and I don't know how to refill my tank.
I have felt sad or miserable

(nodding, tears streaming down her face) Oh, yeah. That's me. I feel sad and miserable a lot of the time. It's like, I'll be sitting there, holding my baby, and I'll just start crying. I don't even know why, it's just... (sobbing) everything feels so overwhelming, and I feel so alone. Even when my partner is there, trying to support me, I just feel like I'm drowning in this sea of emotions. (wiping away tears) And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. Like, I'll be trying to get the baby to sleep, and they'll just keep crying, and I'll feel like I'm failing. Or I'll be trying to make breakfast, and I'll just burn the toast, and I'll feel like I'm a complete failure as a mom. (shaking head) It's just... everything feels so hard, and I feel so... inadequate. (looking down, voice barely above a whisper) And the worst part is, I feel like I'm supposed to be happy. I'm supposed to be enjoying this time with my baby, but instead I just feel... sad. And guilty. Guilty for feeling sad, guilty for not being a better mom. (trailing off, overcome with emotion) Sorry, it's just... it's really hard for me to talk about this. (sobbing)
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nodding, tears streaming down her face) Oh, yeah. I've been crying a lot. It's like, I'll just be sitting there, and suddenly I'll just start sobbing. It's not even always about anything specific, it's just... (sobbing) everything feels so overwhelming, and I feel so sad and alone. And it's not just when I'm by myself, either. I've cried in front of my partner, in front of my family... (shaking head) I just feel like I'm losing control, you know? Like, I'm just this emotional mess, and I don't know how to stop it. (wiping away tears) And it's not just the big cries, either. I've had days where I've just been tearful all day. Like, I'll be feeding the baby, and I'll just start crying. Or I'll be changing their diaper, and I'll just start crying. (sighing) It's just... everything feels so emotional, and I feel like I'm just barely holding it together. (looking down, voice barely above a whisper) And the worst part is, I feel like I'm crying for no reason. Like, I'll be sitting there, and I'll just start crying, and I'll think to myself, "What's wrong with me? Why am I crying?" (shaking head) It's just... it's really hard for me to understand what's going on, and why I'm feeling this way. (sobbing) Sorry, it's just... it's really hard for me to talk about this.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(shaking head) No, that's not something I've thought about. I mean, I've felt really overwhelmed and sad, but I've never thought about harming myself. (pausing, looking down) I just feel like I'm struggling to cope with everything, and I don't know how to make it better. But hurting myself is not something I've considered. (looking up, tears in her eyes) I just want to be a good mom, and take care of my baby, and be happy. I don't want to feel this way anymore. (sighing) I just wish I could find a way to make the sadness and anxiety go away, and just enjoy this time with my baby. (smiling slightly) I love my baby so much, and I want to be the best mom I can be for them.

The patient is experiencing a range of emotional difficulties during the postpartum period, including persistent feelings of sadness, anxiety, and overwhelm. They report difficulty coping with responsibilities, feeling like they are failing as a mother, and experiencing guilt and self-doubt. The patient also expresses feelings of being overwhelmed, tearfulness, and emotional reactivity, which are impacting their daily life and ability to care for their baby.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 27, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>the 'Not at all' option.</sym>, <sym>Hardly at all'.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates a frequent and pervasive pattern of self-blame, suggesting that they blame themselves 'most of the time' for various things, including their baby's crying, their own tiredness, and their partner's stress.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates a high level of anxiety and worry, stating they worry 'all the time' and listing numerous concerns, which aligns with the 'Yes, very often' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient describes frequent and intense episodes of panic, characterized by a racing heart, tight chest, and difficulty breathing, indicating a high level of distress and occurrence of scary or panicky feelings for no very good reason.</sym>, <sym>the guideline option 'Yes, most of the time I haven't been able to cope at all</sym>, <sym>Patient explicitly states they have been having a hard time sleeping due to feeling unhappy and anxious, indicating difficulty sleeping most of the time.</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, most of the time' option, even though the exact phrase isn't used. The patient's emotional expression and description of feeling overwhelmed and inadequate as a mom further support this scoring.</sym>, <sym>The patient reports crying a lot, feeling overwhelmed, and tearful all day, indicating a high frequency of crying due to unhappiness.</sym>)
**Reasoning:** The patient's EPDS score of 27 indicates a high risk for <med>postpartum depression</med>. Their symptoms, including persistent <sym>sadness</sym>, <sym>anxiety</sym>, and feelings of <sym>overwhelm</sym>, are consistent with the <med>DSM-5 criteria for Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med>. The patient's reports of <sym>guilt</sym> and <sym>self-doubt</sym> related to mothering abilities also suggest a need for further evaluation and support. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent appointment with <med>primary care provider (PCP)</med> or <med>mental health specialist</med>
2. Encourage patient to contact <med>emergency services</med> or <med>crisis hotline</med> if experiencing severe symptoms or suicidal thoughts
3. Recommend <med>therapy</med> or <med>counseling</med> to address <sym>anxiety</sym>, <sym>depression</sym>, and <sym>adjustment difficulties</sym>
4. Support patient in developing <med>self-care</med> practices, such as <med>sleep hygiene</med>, <med>exercise</med>, and <med>stress management</med>
5. Facilitate connection with <med>postpartum support groups</med> or <med>online resources</med> for additional guidance and community
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
